How this tone talks (written for the AI)
Keep the relationship, leave room, easy for them to accept. Move things forward without litigating the past — but don\'t silently agree to anything they left vague.
Put the problem on the table, hold the line, neither fight nor fold. Speak in concrete facts, numbers and dates so they see the cost themselves. Stay polite throughout.
State the rule, stop conceding, accept that this may end the relationship. Still only facts and consequences — no profanity, no personal attacks, no threats.
Don\'t commit, don\'t take the bait, keep the decision yours. Short, calm, no explaining, no promises — buy yourself time.

Genuinely receive what they said and move the relationship forward. Praise something specific, add a line of your own — but no flattery and no filler.
Make the thanks concrete: what they did and what it meant to you. Don\'t stop at “thanks”, and don\'t overdo it until it becomes a burden.
Agree cleanly and move things forward. Say exactly what you\'ll do and by when — take it on gladly, but don\'t vaguely promise the parts you can\'t control.
Defuse with lightness and a bit of self-deprecation. Jokes land on the situation, never the person — no sarcasm as a weapon. If it genuinely isn\'t funny, don\'t force it.
For when they\'re hurting. Receive the feeling first; don\'t rush to advice or logic. Talk like a person — no slogans, no breezy “it\'ll be fine”.
Don\'t commit while the information is thin. Ask the one or two things that decide it (what, by when, how much) and put the ball politely back in their court.
Pick the relationship before a tone. “Hard line” to your boss and to your partner are not the same message.
What to keep in mind with this person (written for the AI)

You can\'t opt out of family; anything said harshly you\'ll live with for years. Be direct, set a boundary — but don\'t drag up old grievances or pass judgment on who they are. Settle this one thing; keeping the relationship matters more than winning this round.
Equals, no hierarchy. You can be candid, jokes and self-deprecation are fine — but don\'t use “we\'re close” as licence to decide for them or to overstep.
Feelings weigh more than logic here. Receive how they feel before addressing the thing itself; no old grievances, no character verdicts, no silent treatment or ultimatums.
There\'s a commercial boundary. Hold scope, dates and price; polite but not free. Put in writing whatever needs to be, so a verbal aside doesn\'t become an obligation.

There\'s a power gap; pushing back head-on costs you. Don\'t defy, but don\'t silently accept a request they left vague either. Put cost, schedule and priority on the table and let them choose between options rather than you absorbing it alone.
